root_cause: The Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) library, when initialized with inputMode: true for non-inline datepickers, captures the Tab keydown event on the input element and calls preventDefault(), blocking the default focus traversal behavior.
repair_strategy: Set the VCP inputMode option to false in the datepicker configuration to prevent keyboard event capture, allowing the Tab key to propagate normally for focus movement while preserving mouse-based date selection and programmatic value updates.
expected_accessibility_effect: Restores expected tab order navigation from the date field to subsequent form fields, enabling keyboard-only users to exit the date picker widget as required by WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard.
functional_risks: Direct keyboard date input in the field may not update the calendar display (reliant on click or programmatic updates)
Inline datepickers may lose VCP keyboard navigation if dependent on inputMode=true
Arrow key navigation within the calendar popup may be affected (though not used in this journey)
verification_requirements: Tab key press on focused date field moves focus to next form field (#passengers)
Clicking a date in the calendar updates the input field value correctly
Initial date value (2026-10-22) is properly parsed and displayed on load
Inline datepickers (if present) remain functional for mouse interaction
